context.title: The First Census
context.summary: In the second year after leaving Egypt, Moses counts Israel's men of fighting age, twenty and older, tribe by tribe, totaling 603,550; the Levites are not counted but are set apart to care for the tabernacle.
context.background: This census organizes Israel as an army preparing to march to Canaan. The totals imply a population of perhaps two million, and how to understand such large numbers is debated; some suggest the Hebrew word for 'thousand' can also mean a clan or military unit.

customs.term: By the house of their fathers
customs.note: Israel was organized in layers: tribe, clan and extended family household. People were counted through their family lines.

watchFor: The same formula is repeated for each tribe (vv. 20–43).
Judah is the largest tribe, with 74,600 men (v. 27).
The Levites camp around the tabernacle 'that there be no wrath' (v. 53).

w: he will be put to death

people.name: Moses
people.summary: Drawn (or Egypt. mesu, “son;” hence Rameses, royal son). On the invitation of Pharaoh (Gen. 45:17-25), Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt.

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: Aaron
people.summary: The eldest son of Amram and Jochebed, a daughter of Levi (Ex. 6:20). Some explain the name as meaning mountaineer, others mountain of strength, illuminator.

people.name: Reuben
people.summary: Behold a son!, the eldest son of Jacob and Leah (Gen. 29:32). His sinful conduct, referred to in Gen. 35:22, brought down upon him his dying father’s malediction (48:4).

people.name: Simeon
people.summary: The second son of Jacob by Leah (Gen. 29:33). He was associated with Levi in the terrible act of vengeance against Hamor and the Shechemites (34:25, 26).

people.name: Zurishaddai
people.summary: Rock of the Almighty, the father of Shelumiel, who was chief of the tribe of Simeon when Israel was encamped at Sinai (Num. 1:6; 2:12).

people.name: Judah
people.summary: Praise, the fourth son of Jacob by Leah.

people.name: Amminadab
people.summary: The father of Nahshon, who was chief of the tribe of Judah (Num. 1:7; 2:3; 7:12, 17; 10:14).

people.name: Nahshon
people.summary: Sorcerer, the son of Aminadab, and prince of the children of Judah at the time of the first numbering of the tribes in the wilderness (Ex. 6:23).

people.name: Issachar
people.summary: Hired (Gen. 30:18). “God hath given me,” said Leah, “my hire (Heb. sekhari)...and she called his name Issachar.” He was Jacob’s ninth son, and was born in Padan-aram (comp. 28:2).

people.name: Nethaneel
people.summary: The son of Zuar, chief of the tribe of Issachar at the Exodus (Num. 1:8; 2:5).

people.name: Zebulun
people.summary: Dwelling, the sixth and youngest son of Jacob and Leah (Gen. 30:20). Little is known of his personal history.

people.name: Eliab
people.summary: A son of Helon, and chief of the tribe of Zebulun at the time of the census in the wilderness (Num. 1:9; 2:7).

people.name: Helon
people.summary: Strong, father of Eliab, who was “captain of the children of Zebulun” (Num. 1:9; 2:7).

people.name: Joseph
people.summary: The elder of the two sons of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 30:23, 24), who, on the occasion of his birth, said, “God hath taken away [Heb. ‘asaph] my reproach.”

people.name: Ephraim
people.summary: Double fruitfulness (“for God had made him fruitful in the land of his affliction”). The second son of Joseph, born in Egypt (Gen. 41:52; 46:20).

people.name: Manasseh
people.summary: The elder of the two sons of Joseph. He and his brother Ephraim were afterwards adopted by Jacob as his own sons (48:1).

people.name: Ammihud
people.summary: The father of the Ephraimite chief Elishama, at the time of the Exodus (Num. 1:10; 2:18; 7:48, 53).

people.name: Elishama
people.summary: A prince of Benjamin, grandfather of Joshua (Num. 1:10; 1 Chr. 7:26).

people.name: Gamaliel
people.summary: A chief of the tribe of Manasseh at the census at Sinai (Num. 1:10; 2:20; 7:54, 59).

people.name: Pedahzur
people.summary: Rock of redemption, the father of Gamaliel and prince of Manasseh at the time of the Exodus (Num. 1:10; 2:20).

people.name: Benjamin
people.summary: The younger son of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 35:18). His birth took place at Ephrath, on the road between Bethel and Bethlehem, at a short distance from the latter place.

people.name: Abidan
people.summary: Father of judgment; judge, head of the tribe of Benjamin at the Exodus (Num. 1:11; 2:22).

people.name: Dan
people.summary: The fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s maid (Gen. 30:6, “God hath judged me”, Heb. dananni).

people.name: Ahiezer
people.summary: Captain of the tribe of Dan.

people.name: Ammishaddai
people.summary: People of the Almighty, the father of Ahiezer, who was chief of the Danites at the time of the Exodus (Num. 1:12; 2:25).

people.name: Asher
people.summary: Happy, Jacob’s eigth son; his mother was Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid (Gen. 30:13). Of the tribe founded by him nothing is recorded beyond its holding a place in the list of the tribes (35:26; 46:17; Ex. 1:4, etc.) It increased in numbers twenty-nine percent, during the thirty-eight years’ wanderings.

people.name: Pagiel
people.summary: God allots, a prince of the tribe of Asher (Num. 1:13), in the wilderness.

people.name: Gad
people.summary: Jacob’s seventh son, by Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid, and the brother of Asher (Gen. 30:11-13; 46:16, 18).

people.name: Jethro
people.summary: “The priest of Midian,” Moses’ father-in-law (Ex. 2:18)=Raguel (Num. 10:29).

people.name: Eliasaph
people.summary: Prince of the Gershonites.

people.name: Naphtali
people.summary: My wrestling, the fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s handmaid (Gen. 30:8). When Jacob went down into Egypt, Naphtali had four sons (Gen. 46:24).

people.name: Ahira
people.summary: Brother of evil = unlucky, or my brother is friend, chief of the tribe of Naphtali at the Exodus (Num. 1:15; 2:29).

people.name: Levi
people.summary: The third son of Jacob by Leah. The origin of the name is found in Leah’s words (Gen. 29:34), “This time will my husband be joined [Heb. yillaveh] unto me.”

places.name: Egypt
places.summary: The land of the Nile and the pyramids, the oldest kingdom of which we have any record, holds a place of great significance in Scripture.

places.name: Sinai
places.summary: Of Sin (the moon god), called also Horeb, the name of the mountain district which was reached by the Hebrews in the third month after the Exodus.
